title: migration backlog id-collision error names only one cause; an operator hitting the other reads advice that cannot work
description:
User bug report, relayed by the orchestrator: "In lore CLI during 'lore init' I still get alias collision conflicts when migrating from backlog.md to quest. I assume this is because they both had the said prefix id." Diagnosed jointly with lore-cli, reproducing before theorizing, per the orchestrator's instruction.

Two genuinely different collision shapes exist under the same "Alias collision" error family, confirmed by both sessions independently against the real CLI:

1. GENUINE DUAL CLAIM (this session's repro): the destination quest workspace already holds a live task under an id/alias an incoming backlog record also claims (e.g. both call themselves QCLI-1). Reproduced against real CLI: fresh workspace + quest task create (auto-allocates QCLI-1) + a backlog source with id: QCLI-1 fails migration backlog preview with exit 5. CONTROL: the identical backlog source against a genuinely fresh workspace with zero pre-existing tasks migrates clean -- confirming the cause is specifically a pre-existing destination claim, not something inherent to the source data. --preserve-source-ids --source-family does NOT resolve this (tested directly): it still refuses, now as "Backlog id preservation refused".

2. POSITIONAL RENUMBERING SHIFT (lore-cli's repro, against real backlog 1.50.1 + quest 0.5.0): a dotted subtask's flattening consumes a number and shifts a later positional allocation onto an id an unrelated sibling record already holds (e.g. OPAG-1, OPAG-1.1, OPAG-2 -- flattening OPAG-1.1 can land its fresh id on OPAG-2). --preserve-source-ids --source-family DOES resolve this -- already covered by this repo's own existing test (QCLI-166, test/e2e/migration/backlog-public.test.ts).

DESIGN QUESTION (why isn't a collision auto-resolved during migration?): already settled by this repo's own prior work, QCLI-155 (2026-08-30, Done) -- investigated the identical question, confirmed refusal (not silent overwrite/renumber/merge) is deliberate and tested. Confirmed independently in this investigation: auto-resolving a genuine dual claim would mean silently dropping one side's alias, the exact silent-reference-loss shape this codebase's philosophy guards against everywhere else (PR #223's three silent-data-loss bugs are the local precedent). Not reopened.

THE ACTUAL DEFECT: the error message named only ONE cause and its remedy (positional renumbering / --preserve-source-ids), leaving an operator hitting the OTHER cause (genuine dual claim) reading advice that cannot work for them, with no way to tell which situation they're in. Confirmed --exclude does not exist as an escape hatch (checked the full migration backlog flag set: --source, --backlog-dir, --preserve-source-ids, --source-family, --digest, --actor, --actor-kind, --accountable-human -- no exclude-style flag). The "excluded" field in preview's own JSON output is a different, automatic doc/config/mcp policy (QCLI-134), not an operator escape hatch, and citing it as one would have been its own defect.

Held the interactive-resolver question (an interactive quest init/lore init caller could ask the operator to choose, rather than refuse outright) pending lore-cli's diagnosis of their own flow -- lore-cli found the collision the user most likely hit is #2 above, and that lore init's own flag/wizard path simply never threads --preserve-source-ids/--source-family through to quest's CLI at all, so an operator has no way to reach quest's own already-working fix without abandoning lore's flow. That is lore-cli's fix to make, not quest-cli's, and may make an interactive resolver here unnecessary for the common case -- judging that against what remains after lore-cli's fix lands, not before.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Both real collision shapes are confirmed by direct reproduction against the real CLI before any code changes: a genuine dual claim (a pre-existing destination task and an incoming backlog record independently claiming the same id/alias) and a positional-renumbering shift (a dotted subtask's flattening landing a fresh id on an unrelated sibling's existing id/alias)

The design question of whether migration should auto-resolve a collision is answered by citing this repo's own settled prior decision (QCLI-155) rather than re-litigated, with the added reasoning for why auto-resolving a genuine dual claim specifically would be unsafe

The error message on both the default (positional) and --preserve-source-ids (id-preservation) collision paths names both possible causes and their respective remedies, rather than only the one the original message happened to describe -- verified live that --preserve-source-ids's own refusal message no longer repeats advice that already failed

No fix asserts a non-existent escape hatch: --exclude was checked against the actual flag set and confirmed not to exist, and the preview envelope's unrelated 'excluded' field (QCLI-134's automatic doc/config/mcp policy) is not cited as one

Regression tests cover both collision shapes' exact message text against the real CLI, including the existing QCLI-155/QCLI-166 tests updated for the widened message and a new test for the previously-uncovered --preserve-source-ids dual-claim refusal path

finalSummary:
Fixed. Both known collision-shape messages (the default/positional path and the --preserve-source-ids/id-preservation path) now name both possible causes and their respective remedies, verified live against the real CLI:

Default path (assertAliasesAvailable's wrapper, backlog-public.ts ~line 505-518): now adds a second sentence -- "If instead this exact id is already a live, unrelated claim in the destination workspace, --preserve-source-ids will not resolve it -- rename or remove the conflicting record in the destination, or rename the id in the source, before retrying." -- alongside the existing positional-renumbering sentence, unchanged.

--preserve-source-ids path (previewWithPreservedIds's BacklogMigrationRefusedError, ~line 393): now adds -- "No further flag resolves a remaining id collision here: rename or remove the conflicting record in the destination workspace, or rename the id in the source, then retry." Under preservation mode there is no further flag to suggest (the operator already used the one that exists), so this message states the two manual remedies directly rather than repeating advice already tried.

Both verified live in this repo: a genuine dual claim (fresh workspace, quest task create auto-allocating QCLI-1, then a colliding backlog source) produces the widened default-path message; the same source with --preserve-source-ids --source-family QCLI still refuses, now with the new preservation-path message. A control (identical backlog source against a truly empty workspace) confirmed the collision requires a pre-existing destination claim -- it does not fire on its own.

--exclude does not exist. Checked the full migration backlog flag set directly in source rather than assume: --source, --backlog-dir, --preserve-source-ids, --source-family, --digest, --actor, --actor-kind, --accountable-human. No fix cites it. The preview envelope's "excluded" field is a separate, automatic mechanism (QCLI-134's doc/config/mcp policy), not an operator escape hatch, and is not conflated with one anywhere in this fix.

Design question (auto-resolve vs. refuse) not reopened: cited QCLI-155 (2026-08-30, this repo, already settled this exact question with a passing regression test) as the standing decision, with the added reasoning that auto-resolving a genuine dual claim would mean silently dropping one side's alias -- the same silent-reference-loss shape PR #223's three bugs are this codebase's own precedent against.

Regression tests: QCLI-155's existing case-collision test updated for the widened default-path message (still starts the same way, now continues with the second branch). A new test covers the previously-uncovered --preserve-source-ids dual-claim refusal path end-to-end through the real CLI (questNative), asserting both the default-path message's new sentence and the preservation-path message's new sentence appear, and that a genuine dual claim still refuses (exit 5) even under --preserve-source-ids -- distinguishing it from QCLI-166's existing test, which proves the same flag genuinely resolves the OTHER (positional-renumbering) cause.

Interactive-resolver question (asking the operator to choose, rather than refusing) held per the orchestrator's sequencing instruction, pending lore-cli's fix to their own init flow -- not started here.
